qa_pairs.answer: Early state (Sessions 1–6): Loretta drives herself everywhere including evening commitments, and the family has not raised this directly. The night-driving habit is background to the family's narrative. Shift signal (Session 7): Tanya surfaces that Loretta skipped the evening portion of a church auxiliary meeting because 'she didn't want to be driving that late.' Loretta confirms it in the same session with unusual directness: 'I made a decision. I am not driving after dark anymore. I have given myself that rule. It is my decision and I am telling you now directly. I didn't want a conversation about it. I just wanted it to be my thing.' Trigger: The night misjudgment coming back from a church event (referenced in background — not described in the chat) appears to be the cause; Tanya inferred it from context. Loretta's framing — 'I have given myself that rule' — is notable because it asserts ownership of the decision. It is not a concession to the family or a response to their concern; it is a private judgment she made and then communicated. Evolved state (Session 8): No reference to nighttime events; Loretta's church transport is now covered by arrangements she has made independently.
